headline: 原住民藝術家奪回海灘空間
context: 達魯格族（Dharug）藝術家 Billy Bain 以 11 件陶土雕塑奪回海灘主體性；一位英國父親則描述帶兒子看 Harry Styles 演唱會、在熱浪中被音樂徹底改變的經驗。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: I knew my 11-year-old son would love an evening at Wembley with his favourite star. But nothing prepared me for what it would mean to me The answers to some little questions are hugely revealing. We pass it off as small talk, but asking about somebody’s first anything often reveals all you need to know about who they are today and why. If only I’d understood the implications of buying Wig Wam Bam by Black Lace as my debut music purchase – had known it would shape so many future interactions and realised how ridiculous you feel simply saying those words, even to those too young or cool to be familiar with the full sonic horror. So, to halt generational trauma, when the opportunity came to supply my son with the dream reply to “What was your first concert?” I took him to Harry Styles at Wembley during a thermometer-shattering heatwave. sources.title: I was a whinger, a cynic, a misanthrope. Then I saw Harry Styles live – and I will never be the same again

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: For his upcoming solo exhibition, the Dharug artist has made 11 colourful clay sculptures that represent a counter-image to the bronzed Aussie beachgoer As a teenager in the mid 2000s, artist Billy Bain would ride waves around Sydney’s northern beaches, having travelled the world watching his champion surfer father, Rob Bain , compete. But even though he was minutes from his home in Avalon, he was often made to feel an unwelcome outsider. “I’d be told that I’m not from there, so I need to go in [to shore],” he says, seeing these warnings as veiled threats of violence. “Otherwise, you know, ‘something’s gonna happen to you’.” Continue reading...
sources.title: ‘The beach was and still is an Aboriginal space’: artist Billy Bain on reclaiming the sand and waves

thread_text:
🧵 1/N
📌 文化藝術

兩則文化故事：海灘與演唱會

澳洲達魯格族（Dharug）藝術家 Billy Bain 即將在新南威爾士藝廊舉辦個展，展出 11 件彩色陶土雕塑。他說海灘「一直都是原住民的空間」——但他少年時在雪梨北部海灘衝浪，卻常被要求離開。這次展覽是一種反印象，也是一種奪回。

英國這邊，一位自稱憤世嫉俗的父親帶 11 歲兒子去溫布利球場（Wembley）看 Harry Styles 演唱會，在熱浪天裡，說那一晚徹底改變了他。

—— 本則來自 The Guardian，2026 年 6 月 28 日發佈，讓圖書館員翻譯給你聽。
threads_text:
文化這邊有兩則。

澳洲達魯格族藝術家 Billy Bain 即將舉辦個展，11 件彩色陶土雕塑代表一種反印象——反對「銅色澳洲衝浪客」的刻板形象。他說，海灘「一直都是原住民的空間」，但他年輕時在雪梨北部海灘衝浪，卻常被人要求離開，有時還帶著威脅意味。

另一則輕一點。英國有位自稱憤世嫉俗的爸爸帶 11 歲兒子去溫布利球場看 Harry Styles，正逢熱浪天，卻說那晚徹底改變了他自己。

本則整理自 The Guardian 於 2026 年 6 月 28 日發佈的報導。
voice_text:
藝文這邊有兩則故事，來自不同地方，但都跟空間和認同有點關係。

先說澳洲的。達魯格族（Dharug）藝術家 Billy Bain 即將舉辦個展，11 件彩色陶土雕塑，講的是海灘作為原住民空間的主體性。他說海灘「一直都是原住民的空間」——但他少年時在雪梨北部海灘衝浪，卻常被人要求離開，有時還帶著威脅。這次展覽是他的一個回應。

英國這邊輕一點。一位說自己一向憤世嫉俗的父親，帶 11 歲兒子去溫布利球場看 Harry Styles 演唱會，在熱浪天裡，說那一晚改變了他。
